records.rationale: Full three-path two-hook patch read. Keep per-task dispatch eligibility veto and abnormal-exit notification. Adapt disallow initialization to each examined candidate, including after retry; one task veto no longer suppresses later tasks unless callback independently vetoes them. Native queue locks, remote migration eligibility and retry breather remain exactly LTS after hook removal. Exit notification remains after queuing disable work; native scx_sched_free_rcu_work synchronizes error_irq_work before freeing exit_info, so callback argument lifetime includes its invocation. Callback can run in atomic IRQ-work context and cannot retain raw exit_info beyond callback or assume all mutable state frozen. No actual lifetime race test claimed.

records.rationale: Full backport patch/message and local upstream b7d4b28db7da89de1d03316c4e67b5a47390fcd3 patch read. Unlike pinned LTS tryget/put, use SCX_TASK_READY to admit only tasks prepared by the preceding init loop. Native scx_tasks_lock serializes list iteration against sched_ext_free removal; task rq/pi locking remains native, so no added reference is needed while this loop keeps iterator locks. Removing final put under that list lock also avoids the backport-described possible last-reference release recursing into sched_ext_free and the same lock; the reported deadlock was not reproduced here. Earlier preparation loop still obtains a reference before explicitly unlocking the iterator for init, and drops it outside the iterator locks. Batching drops locks before selecting the next candidate, not while using a selected task. Native lifetime routines are identical; hooks must honor their lock/lifetime context. READY gate is a deliberate adaptation over LTS, not an upstream-presence claim. Host checks cover gate/notification sequencing only, not actual reference counts or deadlock.
